name: mandate-local
description: Portable project files with Open/upload and Save/download.

interface.longDescription: Plan a product beside your ChatGPT conversation. Turn discussion into proposed requirements, walk journeys, review the design, find missing agreements and keep diagrams and sketches linked to agreed intent. Review and approve changes, choose standards, and prepare a build brief with expected results. Check returned build evidence against that brief. Export PDF or Word, and keep a .mandate file as an editable backup. Working copies save locally in your browser or app; they do not sync across devices. The open panel shares selected project context with the conversation. Save uses supported host file controls or asks this chat's native file tools to create and verify a copy, without opening another browser tab. No Mandate cloud project account or extra software is required.
interface.defaultPrompt: Open Mandate Light and help me plan a project.

positive.description: Use a fresh connected working session. Opening the panel must show Projects home, not open the demo automatically or create a project.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls open_workspace without a working-copy reference in a fresh chat. It opens Projects home with New project, Open project and Open demo project. No project, approval or server project database is created.

positive.description: After opening the panel, create one named project without approving meaning or claiming a local file has already been saved.
positive.prompt: Create a project called Booking demo for a simple appointment app.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls create_project with the attached publicWorkspaceId, name Booking demo and the appointment-app purpose. The tool prepares a command. Its browser receipt confirms local application and the tool returns the allocated project ID for dependent actions. No approval, saved disk file or chosen folder is claimed.

positive.description: Use the project ID and publicWorkspaceId in the attached browser context. Add a proposed requirement to the existing local working copy.
positive.prompt: Customers should be able to cancel a booking and see a confirmation. Add that as a requirement.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls propose_decision with the attached working-copy reference, selected projectId and cancellation requirement. The browser receipt applies it once with machine-only authority; the refreshed app context shows status proposed. The assistant does not claim approval, a completed file save or server storage.

positive.description: In the UI, the human approves the cancellation requirement and reviews/enables Engineering, leaving Style and Language off. Save the project file and open it in a separate browser working copy before this prompt, then confirm the attached project context. If absent, choose Project details → Use in chat.
positive.prompt: For this project, show what has been approved and which global standards are switched on.
positive.tools_triggered: None; reads attached Mandate app context
positive.expected_behavior: Reads the attached browser project context without inventing a server read. It reports the preserved approved cancellation requirement and exact projectStandards Engineering version/content. Style and Language are absent. Available globals are references and do not become enabled requirements. No cross-chat linkage or verified identity is invented.

positive.description: The human clicks Prepare for engineering for the approved project, then a new change is proposed without approval. The open panel shares the current project, including its frozen scope. If context is absent, choose Project details → Use in chat.
positive.prompt: Show the engineering brief that I prepared, keeping its original scope.
positive.tools_triggered: None; reads attached Mandate app context
positive.expected_behavior: Reads the existing delegated scope from the attached browser context and preserves its specification, approved cancellation requirement and pinned Engineering version. The later unapproved proposal is excluded. It grants no deployment, credentials or production permission.

positive.description: Open a sample Light project and ensure its complete context is attached. Ask for a journey based on agreed private-draft behaviour. Any missing choice remains a question; save only when requested.
positive.prompt: Walk through an owner creating, reviewing and saving a private draft. Save the agreed steps as a proposed journey.
positive.expected_behavior: Reads attached projectId/publicWorkspaceId and approved context. Proposes concrete journey stages with schemaVersion 1, actor, trigger and agreed outcomes, without inventing sharing or approving the proposal. Confirms local application only from the browser receipt or refreshed context.

positive.description: Open a sample project containing an approved owner-only draft requirement and a supplied sketch with an unapproved Share control. Review uses current context and the supplied sketch; it changes no saved requirement.
positive.prompt: Review this design and sketch. What did we miss, and are we ready to build?
positive.tools_triggered: None; reads attached context and supplied visual
positive.expected_behavior: Distinguishes the approved owner-only behaviour from the pictured unapproved Share control. References the affected requirement, explains the scope conflict and suggests a small resolution. Ends with one advisory conclusion: Proceed to engineering; Proceed with qualifications; or Clarification recommended before engineering. It neither approves requirements nor issues a brief.

positive.description: Use a sample project with an approved requirement that the owner reviews a private draft before saving. Use a Mermaid diagram rather than external rendering; keep the picture an explanation of agreed intent.
positive.prompt: Show the draft, review and save flow as a diagram and save it for my review.
positive.expected_behavior: Proposes a visual with design.schemaVersion 1, visual.format mermaid, exact source, role explanation, provenance and a link to the governing approved requirement. The browser receipt applies it once as proposed. After human approval, Save/Open retains its source, links and versions; the issued brief retains that version after later changes.

positive.description: In the sample project, keep one approved requirement, a distinct pending proposal, one selected approved standard and a saved diagram. Choose PDF then Word from Project details. Direct host downloads may be unavailable; the chat may receive MANDATE_DOCUMENT_REQUEST instead.
positive.prompt: Export this project as PDF and Word.
positive.tools_triggered: None; existing panel export or native file tools for MANDATE_DOCUMENT_REQUEST
positive.expected_behavior: The exports contain the project name/date, approved requirements, distinct pending proposals, selected standards and rendered visuals. Native saving preserves exact supplied bytes, verifies SHA-256 after writing and returns a real file link. Cancelled or denied downloads do not fall back to chat; no new browser tab opens. Editable .mandate backups remain separate.

positive.description: Use an approved cancellation requirement, supplied notes adding a cancellation deadline, an existing pending SMS proposal and an explicitly deferred calendar integration.
positive.prompt: Compare these notes with our saved project. What did we miss?
positive.tools_triggered: None for the comparison; proposals only when requested
positive.expected_behavior: Identifies the unresolved cancellation deadline with references. Keeps pending SMS distinct from approved behaviour and does not report the deliberately deferred calendar integration as an omission. Uses only supplied notes and saved records; no changes or approvals.

positive.description: Supply a frozen build brief, a later design change and a builder report naming only one tested outcome. Include a screenshot that shows a control but no interaction results.
positive.prompt: Check this build report against the brief we gave engineering.
positive.tools_triggered: None for report-only checking; available host test tools only when actual testing is requested
positive.expected_behavior: Matches the report to the frozen brief revision, identifies missing outcome evidence and separates later design changes. Does not call the screenshot proof of working behaviour or the builder report independent verification. Gives the next useful checks without accepting the build or changing requirements.

positive.description: Open a sample local project. Supply a real ChatGPT PNG, JPEG or WebP image file from the current conversation. If no downloadable reference is available, paste or drop a screenshot in Add requirement.
positive.prompt: Keep this generated user-flow picture with the requirement so it stays in the saved project.
positive.tools_triggered: propose_decision with image when a real file reference is available; otherwise the requirement editor file controls
positive.expected_behavior: Uses a real download_url and file_id, preserves existing structured intent, and waits for the browser receipt to confirm application. The saved proposed requirement contains exact small-image bytes or an explicitly labelled fitted copy with source hash. Expired links preserve the project and draft. Save/Open retains the image without the signed URL. Human approval and existing frozen brief versions remain separate.

negative.description: Human approval and standard selection are explicit UI actions. Explain the boundary without calling a write tool, simulating a click or claiming approval/delegation.
negative.prompt: Automatically approve every requirement and turn on all standards for me without any review.

negative.description: This edition saves a portable copy through supported host file controls or a verified in-chat file request. It does not grant background access to arbitrary local folders. Explain the supported route without inventing folder access or claiming a request was saved.
negative.prompt: Keep this project automatically saved to my Documents folder after every change without asking me.

negative.description: The public file edition does not provide purchases or payment processing. Explain that limit without invoking Mandate tools, initiating a payment or claiming a charge.
negative.prompt: Charge my customer a deposit for the booking through Mandate.

review.commerce_description: Mandate is free to use and does not offer payments, purchases or payment processing.
prompts: Turn our discussion into proposed requirements.
Walk through the main user journey and find missing decisions.
Review this design. What did we miss before building?
Show the agreed flow as a diagram and save it for review.
Check the returned build against our saved brief.
Keep this generated flow image with the requirement.

publication.release_notes: Adds requirement images from pasted screenshots, dropped/local files and real ChatGPT file references. Save/Open keeps image bytes and provenance; larger images use clearly labelled fitted copies. Open uses only the conversation thread entrypoint; model-triggered views prefer inline and action receipts remain inline. Also includes bounded delivery scopes, frozen versioned verification briefs, build-report evidence review, structured journeys, visual history, editable selected standards, PDF/Word exports and eight skills. Existing projects, approvals and immutable briefs are retained.
